national.title: ANC fights to keep control of South Africa's key cities after election setback
national.summary: The ANC appears reluctant to replicate its national power-sharing deal with the pro-business DA at the local level.
national.body:
The party that has dominated South Africa for more than 30 years is in a race against time to secure power-sharing deals in most of the country's cities after a massive drop in its support in this month's local elections.

The African National Congress (ANC) suffered its worst result since it came to power in 1994 when South Africa transitioned from the racist apartheid system to democracy.

It won a majority in just one of the country's nine provinces, Limpopo, down from six in the last elections. It won the most votes in just two of the country's eight cities, compared with six in 2021.

At the national level, the ANC is sharing power with its long-time rival, the Democratic Alliance (DA), but while there is still no official announcement, it appears that ANC party officials do not want to replicate this at the local level.

Parties have until 27 November to negotiate and form local governments.

While the ANC saw a massive decline in its support, it still got more votes than any other party, 31%, down from the 46% in the last local election.

But in the country's economic powerhouse, Gauteng province, which includes Johannesburg and Pretoria, the picture is different. The pro-business DA got the most votes in both cities, as well as the province's other main region, Ekurhuleni.

Nationally, the party got 25% of the vote, up from 22% five years ago.

national.title: Rights groups urge sanctions after ICJ finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
national.summary: The International Court of Justice has no power to enforce Thursday's ruling, which orders Myanmar's military-supported government to allow those who fled the violence to return home safely, to pay reparations to the Rohingya Muslims and prosecute those suspected of having committed genocide.
national.body:
Edith M. Lederer, Associated Press Edith M. Lederer, Associated Press

UNITED NATIONS (AP) — Rights groups are calling for military and economic sanctions against Myanmar after the United Nations' highest court, in the first ruling of its kind, determined that its government committed genocide against the Rohingya minority in a brutal 2017 military operation.

WATCH: International Court of Justice finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya

The International Court of Justice has no power to enforce Thursday's ruling, which orders Myanmar's military-supported government to allow those who fled the violence to return home safely, to pay reparations to the Rohingya Muslims and prosecute those suspected of having committed genocide.

Myanmar's government has denied committing genocide, claiming it acted against insurgents, and is considered unlikely to fulfill any of the court's demands. President Min Aung Hlaing, the former military leader, was in charge of the 2017 operation. The court said evidence showed Myanmar forces killed about 100,000 Rohingya.

Khine Khine Soe, the president's spokeswoman, noted the International Court of Justice decision handed down Thursday had been the result of a nine-to-six vote of the judges.

"Not all 15 judges agreed with the decision," she told reporters in the capital Naypyitaw. "So it was not a decision made unanimously. I would say that it was unfair."

While the World Court's rulings are final and legally binding, it has no recourse beyond reporting noncompliance to the U.N. Security Council.

national.title: Federal jury convicts man of starting deadly 2025 Palisades Fire in Los Angeles
national.summary: The man accused of sparking last year's deadly Palisades Fire was found guilty of arson charges Friday after his first federal case earlier this year ended in a mistrial.
national.body:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — The man accused of sparking last year's deadly Palisades Fire was found guilty of arson charges Friday after his first federal case earlier this year ended in a mistrial.

Jurors convicted Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, of lighting a fire on Jan. 1, 2025, that burned undetected deep in root systems before flaring back up Jan. 7, becoming one of the most destructive wildfires in California history. The Palisades Fire killed 12 people as it incinerated entire neighborhoods in Los Angeles and Malibu.

Rinderknecht, with little apparent reaction, gave his attorneys hugs before leaving the courtroom. His father was present for the trial and as the verdict was read.

Rinderknecht pleaded not guilty to federal charges of destruction of property by means of fire and arson. The scope of the first charge was narrowed to only include the Jan. 1 blaze, known as the Lachman Fire, and the second addresses the Palisades Fire. He was convicted on both charges.

Prosecutors continued to pursue the case after Rinderknecht's first jury deadlocked 10 to 2 in favor of acquittal after a two-week trial in June. They dropped a third charge of timber set afire when they filed a new indictment for the retrial.

During the second trial, prosecutors presented a more tightly organized case that presented digital forensic data, expert testimony and Rinderknecht's state of mind in the hours leading up to the fire. They did not focus as much on his resentment toward the rich and powerful to present the crime as arson motivated by "societal revenge" like they previously did.

Prosecutors zeroed in on evidence placing him at the fire's origin area, such as photographs that showed his car parked at the base of a trail leading up to where the fire started and cellphone tower data pointing to his movement on the hill. Fire detection camera images showed the time window the blaze ignited, and experts eliminated any other source of ignition that night, including fireworks.

They established that Rinderknecht was acting erratic and angry in the hours leading up to the fire through the testimony of Uber passengers and texts sent to his girlfriend at the time.

national.title: Mamdani announces plan to close New York's Rikers Island jail by 2032
national.summary: Plans to shutter the troubled facility date back to 2019, when the city council first voted to close it but delays arose over where to place inmates.
national.body:
New York City's official overseeing the closure of the city's most notorious jail hopes a new plan from Mayor Zohran Mamdani will lead to "a moment of transformation" for how people are detained in the largest US city.

Mamdani on Friday unveiled a plan to close the Rikers Island complex by 2032, to build four new jails and drastically reduce the city's detainee population.

Plans to shutter the troubled facility date back to 2019, when the city council first voted to close it by this year. But plans have been delayed over the years in part due to the logistical difficulties over where to place inmates.

Dana Kaplan - who Mamdani appointed as the city's "Close Rikers Czar" told the BBC News channel on Friday that his latest proposal is not just about getting rid of a decrepit facility.

It is also a "generational opportunity" to "build a different type of detention system" and figure out how to detain people more appropriately, she said.

The Rikers Island jail complex is perched on a 413 acre (167 hectare) island between Queens and the Bronx, and has earned a variety of nicknames over the years because of its dilapidated conditions, including Gladiator School and Torture Island. The jail has housed a number of high-profile inmates awaiting trial, including Tupac Shakur, DMX and Harvey Weinstein.

It houses more than 6,500 inmates at a given time. Mamdani hopes to reduce that number to 4,100 - a goal that has been met with skepticism by the New York City correction officers' union.

"[B]uilding a new system that puts an arbitrary cap on the City's available jail beds is ill-conceived, irresponsible and jeopardizes the safety of all New Yorkers, including our Officers," NYC Correction Officers' Benevolent Association said in a statement. "The City cannot keep the jail population at around 4,100 without irresponsibly releasing individuals who committed violent felony charges."

national.title: Fiona's caretakers and fans mourn the beloved hippo after her death at Cincinnati Zoo
national.summary: Born prematurely almost a decade ago and given slim odds of survival, Fiona became not only a source of hometown pride but also a worldwide symbol of hope and inspiration for many.
national.body:
CINCINNATI (AP) — A necropsy on Fiona the hippo showed that the hat she swallowed nearly two weeks ago was caught in the middle of her small intestine, causing her death this week, the Cincinnati Zoo said Friday.

Fiona, whose premature birth and fight for survival captured hearts nearly a decade ago, died Thursday after an attempt to locate the blockage. She was 9 years old.

The hat Fiona ate after it was accidentally flung into her enclosure was so far into her digestive system that no supportive care could have saved her, the zoo said in a statement.

Since her death, Fiona's fans have covered a hippo statue at the zoo with flowers and notes written in crayon. Others left behind watermelons and pumpkins, some of her favorite treats.

Born prematurely almost a decade ago and given slim odds of survival, Fiona became not only a source of hometown pride but also a worldwide symbol of hope and inspiration for many — from teachers to parents to children.

During her visit to the zoo Friday morning, Jessica Grieshop, who often brought her daughters to see Fiona, called the hippo an inspiration for "anyone that was going through hard times."

"The support that we're feeling from all over the world reminds me of the time when everyone pulled together to root for her to survive," said Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike. "She did, and she gave us almost a decade of smiles."

local.body:
Ann Clutter, a lifelong resident of the Brocton, New York area, passed away on November 19, 2026, in Greenville, South Carolina, at the age of 98.

She was born on December 23, 1927, in Clymer, New York, the daughter of the late Ernest and Roberta (Fleichmann) Seavy. Ann grew up with strong family values that remained with her throughout her life, and she carried those values into every role she held as a daughter, wife, mother, grandmother, and friend. She was a graduate of Brocton High School and remained deeply connected to the community she called home for her entire life.

Ann was married to the late William Clutter, and together they built a life centered on family, hard work, and faith. She was a devoted mother to George Clutter, Larry Clutter, Douglas Clutter, Peggy Weary, Patty Delcamp, Paul Clutter, Bernadette Auffhammer, Joseph Clutter, Thomas Clutter, Cathy Deering, and Charles "Chip" Clutter. She was also blessed with many, many grandchildren, great-grandchildren, and great-great-grandchildren, each of whom brought her great joy and pride. She is also survived by her sister, Mary Murphy.

In addition to her parents and husband, Ann was predeceased by her siblings, Robert Seavy, Richard Seavy, George Seavy, John Seavy, James Seavy, Paul Seavy, Medora Arnold, Betty Erdle, Earnestine Wilcox, and Jane Seavy. Her large family was an important part of her life, and she treasured the many memories shared with those she loved over the years.

Ann worked hard throughout her life and was known as a dedicated grape farmer. She also worked for Cliffstar in Dunkirk, New York, where she was respected for her strong work ethic and dependable nature. Her life reflected the values of perseverance, responsibility, and commitment, and she approached each day with quiet strength and determination.

Faith was an important part of Ann's life. She was Catholic and a parishioner at St. Dominic's Church in Brocton, New York, where she found comfort, fellowship, and spiritual guidance. Her faith helped shape the way she lived, and she was known for her kindness, humility, and steady presence among those who knew her.

Ann enjoyed simple pleasures and cherished time spent with the people she loved. She was an avid bingo player and found happiness in the laughter, conversation, and companionship of family and friends. In her later years, she traveled to the homes of her daughters in Pennsylvania and South Carolina, where she continued to enjoy the warmth of family life and the comfort of being surrounded by loved ones.

local.summary: Little did Brian Barmore know in 2018 — when he and a friend dropped by 21 Brix Winery, Portland, on little more than a whim —- that he would one day be working there, learning all about wines, and ultimately earn one of the wine industry’s highest educational honors. local.body:
Little did Brian Barmore know in 2018 -- when he and a friend dropped by 21 Brix Winery, Portland, on little more than a whim --- that he would one day be working there, learning all about wines, and ultimately earn one of the wine industry's highest educational honors.

So impressed with that winery visit, and with the tasting bar specialist, Chelsea, that he met, Barmore applied for a job on the winery's production team. And soon enough, he became head winemaker and ultimately enrolled in the rigorous educational program conducted by the Wine & Spirits Educational Trust (WSET). The program is considered to be the gold standard of education within the industry.

Barmore earned such a very high score in the final unit of the program's Level Four curriculum to qualify for WSET's acclaimed Certification of Merit. Fewer than 10 percent of enrollees reach this plateau. Only 15,000 people worldwide have reached that level since the WSET was founded in 1969.

WSET's Level 4 Diploma in Wines consists of six units. The five units assessed by examination are followed by a dissertation, or a 3,000-word research assignment. Instruction is online through live sessions, each of which is followed by an on-site examination. Barmore easily passed each exam in the three levels on the first try. His dissertation was on orange wines, a white grape fermented on its skin to extract some color and flavor.

Barmore was introduced to the WSET curriculum in 2023 by a friend, Jaret Kelly, a co-worker at the winery who had completed the program's Level 2 (Wine, Spirits, Beer and Sake). Completing that phase fueled Barmore's burgeoning desire to pursue Level 3, which he passed in May 2024, and to ultimately to advance to Level 4 to earn the WSET Diploma.

"As soon as I got out of the classroom, I started looking up the diploma. I knew that was very hard to accomplish (but) that really sparked my interest because I like to do challenging things," Barmore said.

"I fell in love with learning about winemaking, really enjoyed learning about new varieties, new regions and about how winetasters know the differences in wines based on where they're grown," he explained.

Even so, his Level 3 teacher cautioned him, revealing that none of her students have passed the Diploma standard. "Hearing that made me want to do that," he said.

local.summary: Chautauqua County is now represented in a lawsuit challenging the state’s “Local Cops, Local Crimes Act.” The law bans state law enforcement agencies from entering or maintaining 287(g) agreements with ICE, which can deputize local law enforcement to make immigration-related arrests. local.body:
Chautauqua County is now represented in a lawsuit challenging the state’s “Local Cops, Local Crimes Act.”

The law bans state law enforcement agencies from entering or maintaining 287(g) agreements with ICE, which can deputize local law enforcement to make immigration-related arrests. Initially, 15 New York sheriffs signed onto the suit. On Thursday, Chautauqua County Sheriff Jim Quattrone was added to the list along with Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman, who recently lost in his attempt to unseat Gov. Kathy Hochul, and the Nassau County sheriff and police commissioner.

"The proposed amendments could not have been made earlier," attorney Mateo Forero-Norena of the Federation for American Immigration Reform (FAIR) in his memorandum of law supporting adding the new plaintiffs, including Quattrone. "The capacity allegations are being added in light of the concerns articulated in the court's Nov. 4 order. Meanwhile, adding Sheriff Quattrone and the Nassau County parties required completing the necessary arrangements with undersigned counsel and assembling supporting materials after the original complaint was filed. Plaintiffs elected not to seek to add them while the preliminary injunction briefing was underway so as not to complicate that emergency proceeding. This motion is being filed promptly after the Nov. 4 order and before defendants' response to the complaint is due. No discovery has occurred, and the case remains at the pleading stage. Defendants do not contend that the timing of this motion constitutes undue delay. They have taken no position on the proposed amendments."

Under the 287(g) program led by Immigration and Customs Enforcement, police officers can interrogate immigrants in their custody and detain them for potential deportation.Since President Donald Trump took office in January 2025, ICE had expanded the number of signed agreements it has with law enforcement agencies across the country. That prompted Democrats in the state Legislature, with support from Hochul and Attorney General Letitia James, to enact the Local Cops, Local Crimes Act. Hochul and James have defended the law as a way to protect public safety. The state has since taken legal action against Rensselaer County, the lead plaintiff in the suit, to force compliance with the new law.

Prior to 2025, only one of New York’s 62 counties had a 287(g) agreement with ICE. As of July, there were 12 local law enforcement agencies with 287(g) contracts with ICE. In July James sent letters to the 12 local law enforcement agencies in New York that had 287(g) agreements with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), informing them that state law requires they unwind the agreements by August 25, 2026.

local.body:
Chautauqua County government is once again rallying its employees in support of United Way of Chautauqua County, continuing its workplace giving tradition which helps fund local programs and strengthen local communities.

Through their annual payroll pledges, county employees make a gift which goes to support the work of United Way -- connecting their generosity as individuals to the programs and services helping their family, friends and neighbors.

Last year, county employees collectively gave more than $17,000 - a 21% increase over the previous year.

County Executive PJ Wendel has continued to champion the partnership, recognizing the important role county employees play not only as public servants, but as members of the communities United Way serves.

"County employees see the needs of our community firsthand," Wendel said. "Their support of United Way is another way to help make sure local programs have the resources they need to serve our residents. When our employees come together to give, they are making an investment in the people and communities we serve every day."

Last year alone, United Way programs impacted the lives of local individuals 63,249 times -- an impact only possible because of the collective giving of so many workplaces and individuals.

As part of this year's campaign, United Way of Chautauqua County 2026 Campaign Co-Chair Danielle Patti joined the county-level presentation to share more about the impact of local giving -- including a personal connection which shaped her own commitment to United Way.

As a student, Patti received tutoring through a program supported by United Way donations. Years later, she returned to that organization as an employee -- which put her on a path in the education sector, working with children and families in the same types of programs she had once benefited from.

local.body:
ORCHARD PARK -- Ed Oliver bristled at the notion of the Bills’ defensive turnaround being the result of Buffalo spending the past three weeks feasting on backup quarterbacks -- and another on deck with Miami hitting town on Sunday.

“Who cares. I mean, if I got to choose who I could play I guess it would be a starter. But you don’t get to choose,” the defensive tackle said. “All we get to choose is to take advantage of our opportunities.”

The AFC-leading Bills (8-1) have certainly done that over a three-game stretch in which they’ve allowed one touchdown and a combined 28 points. That’s a marked improvement for a defense that allowed 28.5 points per outing through its first six games.

A contributing factor could well be the level of competition, with Buffalo having faced the likes of Baltimore’s Tyler Huntley and Joe Fagnano, Minnesota’s Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer, and New York Jets rookie Cade Klubnik, who took over after Geno Smith was sidelined in Buffalo’s 31-12 win last weekend.

And now come the Dolphins (1-8), with Kyle McCord set to make his second career start in place of Malik Willis.

Bills coach Joe Brady declined to speculate on the injury-filled state of the AFC East’s quarterbacks that also includes New England’s Drake Maye -- so long as Josh Allen is not among them.

A healthy Allen, the NFL’s active leader among QBs with 131 consecutive starts, is why the Bills are once again Super Bowl contenders. And Allen isn’t looking any further beyond Sunday, even with a Thanksgiving night showdown looming against Kansas City.

“This isn’t just a cakewalk. It’s a team that’s hungry. They’re looking to upset,” he said. “And the way their defense is playing gives them a shot every game they’re in.”

LITTLE VALLEY -- A historic building honoring Cattaraugus County’s Civil War veterans is moving closer to rehabilitation and reopening, thanks to $300,000 in grant funding secured by Citizens Advocating Memorial Preservation (C.A.M.P.).

The Cattaraugus County Memorial and Historical Building, located at 302 Court St. in Little Valley, has been the focus of preservation efforts since C.A.M.P. took ownership of the property in 2017. Through the dedication of volunteers led by President Thomas W. Stetz, the nonprofit organization has protected the building from further deterioration, secured historic designations at the state and national levels, and obtained funding to help pay for asbestos abatement and rehabilitation.

The building was listed on the New York State Register of Historic Places in 2025 and added to the National Register of Historic Places on May 12 of that year. The National Register is the nation’s official list of properties considered worthy of preservation.

The organization’s preservation efforts received an early boost in 2023 when the Cattaraugus County Legislature donated $10,000 to help secure the building’s national historic designation.

Additional funding has come from several organizations and agencies. The largest award, $246,750, was received through the New York State Environmental Protection Fund Grant Program for Parks, Preservation and Heritage. C.A.M.P. was notified of the award in December 2025.

In February 2026, the Preservation League of New York State awarded C.A.M.P. a $40,000 Preservation Opportunity Fund grant. The organization was one of only two recipients selected for funding during the 2026 grant cycle.

Caitlin Meives, director of preservation for the Preservation League, praised the group’s efforts to save the building from demolition.

Gary G. Leamer, 73, of Ripley, NY passed away unexpectedly on Monday morning November 16, 2026 at his home.

He was born in Dunkirk, NY on December 3, 1952 the son of the late Ralph and Shirley Leamer.

He is survived by his loving wife of 37 years, Polly (Sherman) Leamer; four children, Lisa Finn of Lancaster, NY, Gary G. (Yolanda) Leamer II Amarillo, TX, Alicia (Greg) Pickens of Amarillo, TX and Tricia Carris of Corry, PA; 13 grandchildren; five siblings, Eileen (Paul) Dorman of Ripley, NY, Earl (Becky) Leamer of Pensacola, FL and Norm (Cheryl) Leamer of Westfield, NY, Glenn (Deanna) Leamer of Notheast, PA and Carol (Chris) Warner of Westfield, NY.

In addition to his parents, he was predeceased by three children, Shari and Charles Finn and Amanda Leamer, a brother, Wayne Leamer and a sister, Ruth Alonge.

Gary was a graduate of Ripley High School "Class of 1971". He proudly served his country during the Vietnam War in the U. S. Army. He worked for the Ed Barger Grape Farm in Westfield, NY retiring after twenty-three years of service.

He enjoyed NASCAR, collecting coins and was well known as an accomplished woodworker. He could create anything out of wood especially furniture and many different types of planters. Strangers would stop by the house to see where these planters were from.

As per Gary's wishes, there will be no public viewing. A Celebration of Life will be held on Sunday, December 6, 2026 at the Ripley Volunteer Fire Dept., 11 S. State St. Ripley, NY from 11-1 PM. The family suggests memorial contributions in Gary's memory be made to the Ripley Volunteer Fire Dept.

Arrangements have been entrusted to the Mason Funeral Home, 37 Clinton St. Westfield, NY. Please share online condolences at www.masonfuneral.

local.title: Erie County water bills going up in 2027 - here's why
local.summary: The ECWA Board of Commissioners approved its 2027 budget, which includes a 5% rate increase and $78.6 million in infrastructure investments.
local.body: Erie County residents can expect to pay more for water in the new year as the Erie County Water Authority moves forward with a major investment in its water system.The ECWA Board of Commissioners approved its 2027 budget, which includes a 5% rate increase and $78.6 million in infrastructure investments.For median residential customers, the increase in water rates means just over $21 more per year, or about $1.77 a month.The quarterly Infrastructure Investment Charge for small-meter residential customers will also increase by $1.68, from $33.33 to $35.01.WATCH: Erie County water bills going up in 2027 - here's whyThe authority said the revenue will help fund system-wide improvements, including the removal of all remaining lead service lines in its service territory by the end of 2027."We're allocating $10 million to the Lead and Copper project because we're going to complete that initiative to get all the lead out of the pipes by the end of 2027," said Joyce Tomaka, chief financial officer for the Erie County Water Authority.Tomaka said the largest portion of the authority's anticipated infrastructure spending will go toward water main projects."We serve a large portion of Erie County, and so our aging infrastructure is something that we've always had to focus on," Tomaka said. "Next year we're ramping back up and getting going on a lot more main projects."Among the major investments included in the 2027 budget:$36.8 million for new water transmission and distribution mains throughout the ECWA system.$12.8 million for upgrades at the Sturgeon Point and Van De Water treatment plants.$10 million to replace remaining lead service lines.$9.8 million for technology upgrades, including cybersecurity improvements.$6.2 million for upgrades to major pump stations.$3 million for new remote radio-read residential water meters.The residential water rates will take effect January 1, 2027. The authority said the investments are part of a broader, nearly $1 billion infrastructure improvement plan extending through 2041.

local.title: BPD commissioner seeks pro bono staffing study amid hiring problems
local.summary: Buffalo Police Commissioner Erika Shields addressed the Buffalo Police Department's ongoing staffing problems again Friday, saying she is seeking a staffing study to determine the needs of the department.
local.body: Buffalo Police Commissioner Erika Shields addressed the Buffalo Police Department's ongoing staffing problems again Friday, saying she is seeking a staffing study to determine the needs of the department.Her comment comes after my investigation, which revealed the department is relying more heavily on overtime to meet minimum staffing requirements. Shields previously told 7 News the BPD needs more police officers, and she reiterated those comments Friday. "We inherited this, and we're gonna clean it up," Shields said. "The department clearly needs more police officers on the street handling 911."Last week she outlined plans to recruit officers given that there has not been a police exam since 2023 and the next one is not scheduled until 2027. She aims to draw officers from Erie County's active list of potential recruits, along with opening the department up to lateral hires from other police departments.Shields told me it is not possible to know how big the department should be overall because a staffing study has never been done — a subject she returned to Friday."I don't think anybody knows with accuracy whether the police department should be 600 people or 900 people," Shields said.WATCH: BPD commissioner seeks pro bono staffing study amid hiring problemsA study would be costly, so Shields is trying to find a workaround."I'm reaching out to try to find one of the more accredited policing institutes to see if we can get a study done pro bono," Shields said.This would emulate a similar study which took place during Shields' time as Chief of Police in Atlanta."We had Georgia Tech PhD students, and they worked on it for about 18 months because the data points you have to compile are so comprehensive," Shields told me. The department is currently budgeted for 813 sworn officers.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. local.title: Genny C., who came to the Seneca Park Zoo almost five decades ago, is in palliative care
local.summary: Veterinary and care teams will focus on maintaining her comfort and well-being.
local.body:
Genny C., the African elephant who's lived at the Seneca Park Zoo since 1979, is receiving palliative care to keep her comfortable as she ages.

Zoo officials say that over the past several months, Genny C. has experienced recurring digestive issues and has had trouble maintaining her weight. She has also shown signs of colic, a potentially life-threatening condition in elephants.

The zoo's veterinary and animal care teams are using therapies such as anti-inflammatories and pain medications to maintain her comfort and well-being.

The zoo says guests who want to see Genny C. should be aware that when she isn't feeling well, she'll likely be in the barn receiving care. At those times, the barn will be closed to the public.

local.title: Welcoming ways to create an inclusive hospitality venue for all
local.summary: Since I began hosting WXXI’s Move to Include podcast, I’ve been thinking about where I can go to catch up with disabled sources and grab a bite to eat. But where?
local.body:
Since I began hosting WXXI’s Move to Include podcast, which delves into disability rights matters through firsthand perspectives and candid conversations, I’ve been thinking about where I can go to catch up with sources and grab a bite to eat.

And then my mind goes blank. Where are the inclusive dining spots?

Places where someone using a wheelchair can roll up and get through the door without hassle. Where a blind person can read the menu. Where someone with an assistive communication device can place their order and take care of the bill without being made to feel like a nuisance. Where the sound doesn’t ricochet off the walls like the inside of a tin can, so someone who is hard-of-hearing or neurodivergent can carry on a conversation without pain. Where someone with a chronic illness or compromised immune system can feel welcome.

Nearly 30% of adults in the U.S. have a disability, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention . The CDC defines disability as “any condition of the body or mind that makes it more difficult for the person with the condition to do certain activities and interact with the world around them.”

The Move To Include Podcast The Move To Include Podcast puts the voices of people with disabilities at the center of the conversation about inclusion... But there’s another way to look at it: the social model of disability, credited to researcher Mike Oliver. The idea is that a significant aspect of limitations is determined by the blueprint of the built world around us, and people’s attitudes toward disability.

“It is society which disables physically impaired people. Disability is something imposed on top of our impairments by the way we are unnecessarily isolated and excluded from full participation in society,” Oliver wrote in the textbook, “ Implementing the Social Model of Disability: Theory and Research .”

If disability is partly determined by design, then what are the barriers? And what are some ways to alleviate that divide?

Not just meeting Americans with Disabilities Act regulations, which many advocates argue is the bare minimum for accessibility standards (not to diminish how monumental the ADA was when signed into law in 1990), but putting forth best practices in universal design and inclusive social dynamics.

local.title: Feds abandon plans for Border Patrol station in downtown Rochester
local.summary: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is forgoing plans to convert space in the Kenneth B. Keating Federal Building in downtown Rochester into a Border Patrol station, Congressional Democrats say.
local.body:
U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is forgoing plans to convert space in the Kenneth B. Keating Federal Building in downtown Rochester into a Border Patrol station.

Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand, and House Rep. Joseph Morelle announced the stoppage on Friday, saying the General Services Administration, which oversees the Keating Federal Building, notified the Western District of New York Federal Court that CBP withdrew its request and will explore other options.

“This is a major victory for the people of Rochester who made their voices heard and refused to accept the Trump Administration’s reckless plan to bring immigration detention cells into the heart of our downtown,” Morelle said in a news release. “I’m grateful to Senator Schumer and Senator Gillibrand for their partnership in fighting this proposal, and I will continue fighting to protect our community from Donald Trump’s cruel immigration agenda.”

CBP has expressed interest in moving downtown since 2019 and included the project in its 2025 budget request. Border Patrol planned to convert the space into offices, with at least three temporary holding cells, plus K9 kennels and other features.

The proposal faced major opposition from congressional leaders, residents, and elected officials citing concerns and what they described as inaccurate or incomplete information that the administration released to the public in early May.

In an email to WXXI News, a CBP spokesperson said that after an evaluation, the downtown federal building didn't meet the agency's operational requirements.

"CBP is currently evaluating alternative courses of action to meet our facility operational requirements in the area," the spokesperson wrote.

Editor's note: the story has been updated to include a statement from CBP.

local.title: Wayne County supervisors appoint new health director
local.summary: The Board of Supervisors approved Jennifer Rodriguez’s appointment at its meeting this week.
local.body:
The Board of Supervisors approved Jennifer Rodriguez’s appointment at its meeting Tuesday morning.

Rodriguez currently is director of Livingston County Health, where she has served since 2013. She succeeds Diane Devlin, who retired in March. Deputy Director Kerry Van Auken has been directing the agency since Devlin’s retirement.

Rodriguez will be paid nearly $166,000. She starts her new position Jan. 4.

She said her decision to take the Wayne position “is rooted in my longstanding passion for public health and my commitment to improving the health and well-being of the communities I serve.”

Rodriguez said she oversaw multiple areas of public health and community services in Livingston County, “which provided me with invaluable leadership experience and a broader understanding of the challenges facing rural communities.” In October, she took on the additional role of interim director of community mental health services in Livingston County following the resignation of Sarah McCumiskey.

She explained that the Wayne County job allows her “to return my full attention to core public health services, preventive health care, and the essential work of improving population health outcomes.”

“At the heart of my decision is something very simple: I believe deeply in the power of prevention, the importance of accessible healthcare, and the ability of local public health departments to make a lasting difference in people’s lives,” Rodriguez continued. “I am grateful for my years in Livingston County and enthusiastic about beginning this next chapter serving the residents of Wayne County. … I am genuinely excited to join Wayne County, learn from its residents and community partners, and work alongside its dedicated public health professionals. I see this transition as an opportunity for both professional growth and a renewed focus on the work that first drew me to public health.”

Rodriguez was named a Women of Excellence honoree by the Rochester Business Journal in 2021. The RBJ said the program celebrates “high-achieving women across the Greater Rochester area for their professional accomplishments, community involvement, and commitment to mentoring.”

entertainment.title: Why Mariska Hargitay Considered Quitting Law & Order: SVU - And What Stopped Her
entertainment.summary: Plenty of major actors have left "Law & Order: SVU" before, but the show nearly lost its most notable actress after 27 seasons of leading the show.
entertainment.body:
Virginia Sherwood/NBC Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover "Law & Order: Special Victims Unit" wouldn't be what it is if it weren't for Captain Olivia Benson (Mariska Hargitay) policing the streets of New York. Yet, there was a time that the cop drama almost lost its leading lady. After her fellow co-star Chris Meloni (aka Detective Elliot Stabler) departed "Law & Order: SVU" in 2011, Hargitay became the sole protagonist of the series and wasn't able to expand her horizons as a performer. She considered walking away from "Law & Order: SVU" during Season 25 to pursue other opportunities within different genres. Despite showing her comedic chops during her short-lived role in "Seinfeld," the actor rarely got to step out of her iconic character and display her sense of humor.

In a conversation with Julianna Margulies ( who previously quit "ER" in Season 6 ), Hargitay said she had thought of leaving the Dick Wolf procedural but admitted she wasn't ready to say goodbye. "Because I loved it," she explained in an interview with Variety . "And then I got to do all this other stuff, and that's why I don't think about leaving right now." Hargitay did get the chance to branch out without having to let go of the badge, though. She directed a 2025 documentary titled "My Mom Jayne", where she revisited her late mother's legacy. It won two Emmys, and it even helped lead to NBC choosing Hargitay to host the 2026 awards ceremony. The actor also made her Broadway debut with "Every Brilliant Thing," a solo play that is both hilarious and life-affirming. Hargitay played a nameless protagonist who chronicles every brilliant thing in the world to cheer up those around her and herself.

His most recent appearance was tied to a conviction from one of their earlier cases. The duo is forced to consider whether the person they arrested was indeed guilty of raping and murdering a young nun. As they head upstate and interrogate people who knew the victim, Benson and Stabler have a long discussion about their shared history and ponder the mistakes they've made while handling this case.

Fazekas told The Hollywood Reporter that she sought to make "an old school Benson and Stabler episode" to commemorate the show's milestone. Although fans have been rooting for the characters to get together, the showrunner believes that the episode's final moments show that both of them still have a lot of work to do before taking that next step in their relationship. "Is there time down the line? Maybe, but I think he's got some work to do. entertainment.title: Quote Of The Day By Judi Dench: 'Ask Me What I Did Yesterday And I Couldn't Tell You, But...'
entertainment.summary: Famous for Shakespeare plays and 007 movies, Judi Dench has a unique perspective on childhood memories now that she's more than 90 years old.
entertainment.body:
Denis Makarenko/Shutterstock Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Judi Dench is a generational talent who has routinely graced the stage and screen since her professional debut in 1957. Dench starred in a string of Shakespearean plays like "Hamlet" and "Macbeth" in these early years, establishing herself as a notable theater actor for the National Theatre Company and the Royal Shakespeare Company, before branching into film and television.

Dench, of course, gained mainstream popularity after playing M in "GoldenEye," a role she reprised in eight more "James Bond" films. The actor won an Academy Award for her role in "Shakespeare in Love." She has also starred in "Chocolat," "The Chronicles of Riddick," "Pride & Prejudice" (2005), "Pirates of the Caribbean: On Stranger Tides," and "The Second Best Exotic Marigold Hotel."

Other prominent projects include "Mrs. Brown," "Notes on a Scandal," and "Belfast." Dench also appeared in Kenneth Branagh's 1996 adaptation of Shakespeare's "Hamlet." She has earned a Tony, and two Golden Globes, along with several BAFTAs and Olivier Awards.

Dench brings robust expertise and exceptional talent to both stage and screen, which is why she is today's quote of the day.

Static Media "Ask me what I did yesterday and I couldn't tell you, but I can recount in vivid detail what I did over 80 years ago — the holidays, the friendships and the mischief I got up to at school."

The above quote is from Dench's 2026 interview with People . On the topic of childhood remembrance, Dench said that she is "amazed" at how much she remembers from that time. While comparatively recent events often escape her mind, Dench is able to vividly look back at her childhood and feel the warmth shared with friends.

Speaking about her childhood, Dench recalled her troublemaking ways. "My God, I was a real tearaway — setting off fire extinguishers and tying my fellow classmates to their chairs. I'm surprised I wasn't expelled," the actor mused. There's genuine fondness in the way Dench looks back on her mischief-laden school years, and how they remind her of a simpler time.

Dench also shared her early ambition to become a ballerina, and how she eventually became invested in acting on the stage. "My earliest ambition was to become a ballerina, but when my father pointed out I'd have to retire by the time I was 40, I decided it probably wasn't for me," Dench added.

“Dirty Dirty Disco” was released Sept. 10 as the first collaboration between the Melbourne-formed dance-rock group and Minogue, pairing her with Rogue Traders vocalist Natalie Bassingthwaighte .

“When I heard the original version of ‘Dirty Dirty Disco’ I was instantly in love with the record,” Mashd N Kutcher’s Matt James said. “What an awesome link up between two icons. The remix came together super quickly and was all about the vibes, a cut to spin late nights.”

Minogue said she had wanted to work with the duo for some time. “I couldn’t be more happy that he was digging this track and wanted to remix it and spin it in his sets,” she said.

Minogue, the younger sister of Kylie Minogue , charted on Billboard’s Top Dance Albums with 2003’s Neon Nights, which peaked at No. 17. Rogue Traders were formed by Ash and Steve Davis, with Bassingthwaighte joining in 2005; their biggest hit, “Voodoo Child,” led their second album, Here Come the Drums.

entertainment.title: Phil Collins Says Cher Sang His ‘We Are the World’ Line at Live Aid After He Left Early
entertainment.summary: In a SiriusXM interview marking his second Rock Hall induction, Collins recalls the Concorde flight, meeting Cher mid-air, and discovering she'd taken his spot.
entertainment.body:
Phil Collins has told the story of how Cher ended up singing his line in the “We Are the World” finale at Live Aid — because he was too tired to stay.

Speaking in a takeover of SiriusXM ’s Classic Rewind marking his induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame as a solo artist, Collins recounted the 1985 double-header that took him from Wembley to Philadelphia in a single day, and the chance encounter that followed. Related Mashd N Kutcher Remix Rogue Traders and Dannii Minogue's 'Dirty Dirty Disco' 2026 CMA Awards Jump to 7-Year Ratings High Nick Cannon Hospitalized Amid Lupus Battle: 'Pray for Me, Y'all!' Explore Cher Eric Clapton Genesis See latest videos, charts and news

Collins said he had asked to drum for Eric Clapton and Robert Plant , having recently worked with both, and was told they were playing the American leg. A promoter he believes was Harvey Goldsmith then raised the possibility of doing both shows by Concorde. “I said, ‘Oh, okay. Well, I’ll do that then,’” Collins recalled, asking whether anyone else was attempting it “because I thought that was a bit show-offy.” The Power Station were also booked to do it, he said, but pulled out.

Cher was on the same Concorde. “Cher came up to me in the middle of the flight and said, ‘What’s going on? What’s happening? Obviously something is happening,’” Collins said. He told her about Live Aid, and she asked if he could get her in. “I said, ‘Well, you’re Cher. You know, you don’t need me here to get you on. Just turn up.’”

After playing his own set and drumming with both Led Zeppelin and Clapton, Collins was scheduled for the “We Are the World” closer but left. Collins said he was “so knackered” that he told himself, “I can’t do this. I’m not going to make it till the end of the show.” He added, “So I said, ‘Get someone else. I’m going back to New York.’” Back in New York, he turned on the television to find the finale already underway. “And guess who was singing my line?” he said. “Cher.”

Collins also discussed his friendship with Clapton, whom he first met through Scottish singer-songwriter John Martyn, when the pair drove to see Clapton in Guildford. The two lived near each other in Surrey and became close; Clapton was best man at Collins’ second wedding. Collins went on to produce Clapton’s Behind the Sun , recorded in Montserrat, after, Collins believes, Clapton’s engineer Tom Dowd suggested him.

“I encouraged him to write, because his album before the one I did, Money and Cigarettes , was a little laid-back and didn’t jump out the speakers,” Collins said. “He was getting lazy, in other words.” He co-produced the follow-up, August , with Dowd, and toured with a band including Nathan East and Greg Phillinganes. “We used to call it ‘The Heaven Band’ because we all loved it,” Collins said. “That was just the best band I’ve ever been in.” He said the pair have been in touch recently: “He’s the best guitarist I’ve ever played with.”

entertainment.summary: Columbus directed the first two films in the "Home Alone" franchise.
entertainment.body:
“Home Alone” director Chris Columbus was seemingly unaware that a sequel to his beloved holiday classic is in the works, in comments delivered just prior to its announcement.

“Catherine, as I’ve always said, is 50% of ‘Home Alone,’” the director told Variety in comments published Friday, referencing the movie’s co-star Catherine O’Hara, who played Kate McCallister — the mother to Macaulay Culkin’s Kevin McCallister — in the film.

“There’s the yin and yang of ‘Home Alone’: Catherine O’Hara and Macaulay Culkin. Without those two in the film, there is no film, because they create the emotional epicenter of that film,” Columbus reasoned.

Sources told the outlet that the 68-year-old director “had no knowledge” of the project.

Columbus — who also directed “Home Alone 2: Lost in New York” in 1992 — told the publication that he couldn’t rule out a potential return for the franchise.

“I think you potentially could still entertain the idea of doing another ‘Home Alone’ with the cast,” he told the outlet.

“Not any of these ridiculous follow-ups to the first,” Columbus added. “And I only say ridiculous because it’s weird with filmmakers. They don’t understand why that cast works so well. It’s always about the cast.”

Deadline reported the same day that Culkin, now 46, is attached to star in a long-awaited sequel at Disney-owned 20th Century Studios, and it’s being based on the actor’s concept of Kevin having grown into a father.

entertainment.title: Man Found Guilty of Igniting Blaze That Became the Devastating Palisades Fire
entertainment.summary: Jonathan Rinderknecht was found guilty for his role of intentionally starting the blaze that would become the most destructive wildfire in Los Angeles history
entertainment.body:
A jury found a former Los Angeles resident guilty of starting what became the deadly Palisades Fire of January 2025, the city’s most destructive wildfire in its history.

Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, was convicted of one count of destruction of property by means of fire and one count of arson affecting property used in interstate commerce. Federal prosecutors accused Rinderknecht of intentionally starting the original blaze, known as the Lachman fire. While the initial fire was quickly suppressed, unbeknownst to firefighters and other authorities at the time, embers of it continued to burn underground. On Jan. 7, heavy winds reignited the fire, causing it to surface and spread. The ensuing Palisades fire was one of the most destructive wildfires in Los Angeles history, killing 12 people and decimating 23,448 acres of land and nearly 7,000 structures across the Pacific Palisades region.

“Twelve people lost their lives and thousands lost their homes because of Jonathan Rinderknecht’s malicious conduct,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche in a statement. “Thanks to the persistence and hard work of our prosecutors in the Central District of California, he will be held accountable.”

“Jonathan Rinderknecht deliberately ignited a fire that killed 12 people and devastated an entire community,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli. “We were determined to hold him accountable, and today’s guilty verdict delivers a measure of justice for the families who lost loved ones and the thousands whose lives were upended.”

After a federal jury in June deadlocked in favor of acquittal in Rinderknecht’s first trial in June, federal prosecutors narrowed their case to charge him with the two arson-related felonies rather than the three charges in the mistrial.

“It’s amazing to me that I made that decision so young, and that thank God Jeffrey was OK with it,” she recalled on a November 2025 episode of the Good Hang with Amy Poehler podcast. “I just can’t imagine my life any other way I’ve done it. entertainment.title: '70s Hit Sci-Fi Show The Bionic Woman Was Inspired By A Classic Horror Movie
entertainment.summary: The influence of this classic horror movie is clear to see in The Bionic Woman, and it is one that totally makes sense when you think about it.
entertainment.body:
In the first issue of Starlog magazine, Johnson recalled meeting Harve Bennett, the producer on ABC's "Six Million Dollar Man." Bennett mentioned that he was in need of scripts for the sci-fi series. "I suggested the 'Bride of Frankenstein' — give him a bionic woman; and everyone liked the idea," Johnson recalled. "I went home and wrote the script in a week."

"Bride of Frankenstein," James Whale's 1935 follow-up to his classic Universal horror movie "Frankenstein," famously introduced Elsa Lanchester's streak-haired mate to Boris Karloff's monster. (The monster requests that Dr. Frankenstein make him a woman in Mary Shelley's original novel, but no actual bride gets resurrected.)

The Bionic Woman, Lindsay Wagner's Jaime Sommers, made her debut in season 2 of "Six Million Dollar Man" and would headline her own three-season show and go on to win an Emmy . Jaime and her cyborg counterpart Lee Majors' Steve Austin , had a long relationship that culminated in marriage after a series of TV movies. This was a much happier ending than Frankenstein's Monster and the Bride got in their movie; the Bride hisses at the Creature and then he blows them both up shortly after they meet.

In the pilot episode of "The Six Million Dollar Man," which premiered on March 7, 1973, Steve's first words upon waking up from the surgery that turns him into a cyborg are "Dr. Frankenstein, I presume?," a riff on the famous Henry Morton Stanley quote.

Of course, Steve Austin and Jaime Sommers are quite different characters than their undead counterparts. Jaime, especially, couldn't be further from the Bride in terms of personality. Namely, she has one. The Bride, at least in her debut appearance, is terrified and semi-feral in her brief second life.

"I designed her as the complete woman," Kenneth Johnson told Starlog . "She is not self-conscious, or a second-class citizen. She is a very together woman." Johnson added that Jaime helped inject some much-needed humor into "The Six Million Dollar Man."

entertainment.body:
Courtesy of Starz Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover This post contains spoilers for "Outlander: Blood of My Blood" Season 2, Episode 9. Proceed accordingly.

There are far bigger, deadlier, and fate-twisting events that happen in this week's "Outlander: Blood of My Blood ." But when I get some time to discuss Episode 9 with series star Sadhbh Malin, my first question is about a tiny — yet crucial! — moment that passes between her Jocasta and Rory Alexander's Murtagh during the hour.

The interaction comes in the aftermath of John Cameron's (Alastair Mackenzie) death, which happened as Murtagh fought the man after stopping him from raping Grace (Ruby Fubara). Jocasta knows Murtagh loves Grace, but that doesn't dampen Lady Cameron's own feelings for him.. And their mutual regard for each other is evident as he grabs her hand during a brief, emotional conversation in the threshing barn.

In a show and franchise known for its love scenes, the touch is extremely chaste. But it was filled with everything the characters haven't said to each other over the course of the past two seasons, and therefore we demanded that Malin tell us everything she could about shooting the scene.

"Oh my God, yeah," she says, breaking into a wide smile. Watching it myself this time around, my heart started beating [faster] when I saw it. Because they're, as individual characters, in such different places at that moment. They're actually really far away from each other."

She brings up the characters' first interaction in the show, in Season 1, in which a handkerchief played a pivotal role. "There's a moment where their hands brush each other, and I guess that's now like a recurring thing that I think is so beautiful and so intimate in a world where there is little physical intimacy" between people who aren't married.

Courtesy of Starz Jocasta and Murtagh's biggest scene together so far came in Season 1's "Needfire," in which a drunken and heartbroken Murtagh (over Ellen this time) kissed Jocasta at a Beltane celebration. It... didn't end well. Malin says this week's episode hit her the same way.

The barn conversation "really stuck out for me as well, watching it back, because I think you can see how painful it actually is for her in that moment. When it first happens in Season 1, and then when it happens at Beltane... they're connected in some way," she explains. "But then, when it happens here, it feels actually so much more heartbreaking, because it means very different things for both of them. You can see her heart just, like, shattering and melting."

Kirk on the original "Star Trek" series was complete, William Shatner landed a small role in the TV world of crime and detectives. The actor guest-starred on one episode of "Mannix" in 1973, four years after his last live-action appearance as Captain Kirk on television.

In Season 6, Episode 21, titled "Search for a Whisper," Shatner portrayed Adam Langer, a rich businessman planning to run for governor who hires private detective Joe Mannix (Mike Connors) to dig up any dirt that could be used to wreck his campaign. Mannix doesn't find any skeletons in Langer's closet at first, but he later suspects someone is following him. Meanwhile, several people he interviews suffer mysterious deaths. Forced to go behind his client's back to uncover the truth, Mannix's seemingly routine case ends up a lot more scandalous and dangerous than expected.

A popular CBS crime series that ran for eight seasons from 1967 to 1975, "Mannix" helped set the standard for detective shows during its run. Now, more than five decades after "Mannix" aired its final episode, the drama series is still considered among the best TV shows of the 1960s .

CBS William Shatner's "Mannix" stint saw him play an amiable man on the surface with a lot to hide, giving him one of many opportunities to show his range outside of the sci-fi genre. In fact, the earlier days of Shatner's 70-plus-year acting career saw him make guest appearances on other classic crime shows like "Columbo," "Hawaii Five-O," and "The Man from U.N.C.L.E." A few years before his "Mannix" episode aired, Shatner played a murderer on ABC's "The Fugitive" .

Later in the 1980s, Shatner headlined the cop procedural "T.J. Hooker," which made him appreciate the hard work that police officers and detectives do in the real world. "I enjoyed it very much. It was well written. Ex-policemen were on it. I got to know the police force. I have great admiration for so many of the men and women who are doing that duty," Shatner said in an interview with TV Insider .

Shatner returned to the "Star Trek" franchise as Captain Kirk in "Star Trek: The Animated Series" in 1973, the same year as his "Mannix" episode, and then again in 1979 for "Star Trek: The Motion Picture." Even though the actor will always be remembered as a sci-fi legend, he certainly had a knack for playing someone embroiled in a crime investigation. entertainment.title: Beverly Hills, 90210 Alum Kimmarie Johnson’s Cause of Death Revealed
entertainment.summary: Authorities have determined what led to Kimmarie Johnson’s death. Two weeks after the actress, who appeared in Beverly Hills, 90210 and Dude, Where’s My Car?, died Nov. 3 following what her niece...
entertainment.body:
Authorities have determined what led to Kimmarie Johnson ’s death.

Two weeks after the actress, who appeared in Beverly Hills, 90210 and Dude, Where’s My Car? , died Nov. 3 following what her niece described as a “heart event,” her cause of death was determined to be cardiopulmonary arrest, according to a death certificate obtained by People , who listed her age as 59.

While a heart attack—medically referred to as myocardial infarction—is the result of a blocked artery, cardiopulmonary arrest—or cardiac arrest—is when the heart stops beating and is unable to effectively pump blood to the body, according to the Cleveland Clinic .

Johnson’s death certificate also listed an underlying cause as metastatic granulosa cell ovarian tumor with peritoneal carcinomatosis, meaning the rare type of ovarian cancer she had spread to her abdominal area, according to the Mayo Clinic .

After her death, Johnson’s niece Rhonda Scott reflected on the joy her aunt brought into the world.

“She radiated a light so strong and bright,” Scott told People in an interview published Nov. 5. “People who came in contact with her felt nothing but positive energy. We will miss her tremendously and will continue to honor her life forever.”

Johnson graduated from Wilkinsburg High School in Pittsburgh in 1985 before studying at California University in Pennsylvania. She won the title of Miss Pennsylvania USA in 1993 and was subsequently a finalist at the Miss USA pageant.

She later moved to New York City and then Los Angeles, where she pursued a career in modeling. While Johnson found small roles on the big screen over the years, she launched her skincare brand SkinGlow by Kimmarie in 2011 and continued to model until her death.

entertainment.title: 5 Best Sitcom Moms Of The '60s, Ranked

ABC/YouTube Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover From "Modern Family" to "Leave It to Beaver," the family sitcom remains one of the most enduring threads in American television fare. This fact rang especially true in the 1960s, when shows like "The Beverly Hillbillies" and "The Munsters" regularly mesmerized households across the country. But the land of the 1960s sitcom was far from business-as-usual. In the wake of the enduring 1950s craze around "I Love Lucy," female characters were slowly moving to television's forefront, and TV writers were freer than ever to experiment with onscreen representations of motherhood.

Out of all the archetypical parts that make up the family sitcom , the role of the mother often imbues audiences with the greatest amount of nostalgia. For many young viewers, characters like Louise Jefferson and Edith Bunker offered a warmly supportive presence that they could reliably find in the same place at the same time, week after week. While this warmth could be found in a wide range of sitcom moms across the '60s, there are a handful of women who especially stand out for the irreplaceable importance they brought to their surrounding shows. Here are five of the best sitcom moms, ranked.

CBS/YouTube The spiritual sequel to "I Love Lucy ," "The Lucy Show" continued Lucille Ball's trailblazing path through the television industry, bringing her talents to the role of the wacky widowed mother Lucy Carmichael. While Lucy Carmichael was a caring mother to her son and daughter, she was also constantly embroiled in harebrained schemes of her own making. Whether she was lying about being an expert duck hunter or trying to achieve eternal youth, one thing was clear to 1960s audiences: Lucy was one of television's funniest, most outrageous mothers.

Since later seasons of "The Lucy Show" shied away from motherly depictions of its protagonist by writing out both of her children, Lucy Carmichael receives last billing on this particular list. But the character's lasting legacy feels undeniable. By placing the traditionally tragic figure of the single mother at the center of her own comedy, "The Lucy Show" arguably paved the way for more empowering portrayals of all kind of TV moms . Throughout the show's early stages, Lucy Carmichael served as living proof that mothers could be compelling television characters — and laugh-out-loud funny to boot.

"It looks like now I might have to write [a script for another movie.] It wouldn't be a final one because everybody loves it. Nick Cannon revealed Friday (Nov. 20) that he’s been hospitalized amid his battle with lupus, and he’s asking fans to keep him in their prayers.

“#LupusWarrior,” Cannon wrote in his caption, soundtracked by Donny Hathaway’s “A Song for You.” The accompanying photo finds the father of 12 undergoing a series of medical tests while lying in a hospital bed and wearing a PPE mask.

He added in the photo: “This [world emoji] can definitely take a lot out of you. Pray for me y’all!”

Cannon posted a clip to his Instagram Story , as he seemingly prepared to undergo a CT scan. “Have you had a CT before?” a medical professional can be heard asking him off-camera.

Billboard has reached out to a rep for Cannon for further information about his hospitalization.

The Wild ‘n Out creator was diagnosed with the autoimmune disease back in 2012. According to Mayo Clinic , “Lupus is a condition in which the body’s immune system attacks its own tissues and organs. This is called an autoimmune condition. Lupus causes swelling and irritation, called inflammation, that may affect joints, skin, kidneys, blood cells, brain, heart and lungs.”

Among his myriad business commitments, the 46-year-old has been traveling for his Wild ‘n Out Live: The Next Generation tour, which continues Saturday (Nov. 21) at Houston’s Toyota Center. It’s still unknown if he will appear at the show.

In September, Cannon announced he was set to give fans an inside look at his chaotic family life through a Netflix docuseries, which is set to air this winter.

entertainment.title: Kylie Cantrall Talks ‘Bold, Grown & Messy’ New Music, How Her Disney Fans ‘Coexist’ With Growing Audience
entertainment.summary: The Disney alum gets candid about her new music era at intimate Moxy Hotels Check-In Sessions.
entertainment.body:
Nestled into a corner of the Moxy Hotel in downtown L.A. this week, Kylie Cantrall sat down with Billboard to chat about her sold-out headlining solo tour, her songwriting process and her new era, post-Disney’s Descendants franchise.

Growing up in the nearby Valley, Cantrall starred in her breakout role as Red in Disney’s Descendants in 2024, and is now the release of her Valley Girl Problems EP on July 24 marks a new chapter for the Venezuelan-American artist.

With her Valley Girl Problems Tour wrapping up last month and anticipation building for her upcoming Jingle Ball LA performance in December, Cantrall surprised fans with an intimate acoustic performance at the Moxy. Reaching out directly to her fanbase through a text message, she offered a more personal, stripped-down evening and a chance to connect in a smaller setting.

Stepping out of her Descendants era, the former Disney star has found a strong connection with listeners through her solo music, which explores themes of teenage heartbreak, friendship breakups and the growing pains of finding yourself. “ Valley Girl Problems was what I was going through at that time. Discovering myself and opening up about the trials and tribulations, and the messier parts,” she says.

Cantrall has described the nine-track project as a reintroduction to herself as an artist, leaning into the very Valley Girl stereotype that has become part of her identity. After landing her Disney breakout role at the age of 17, Los Angeles became an essential part of her journey into the entertainment industry. Rather than shy away from her roots — Valley Girl vocal fry and all — she’s embracing the persona as a reflection of who she is.

That sense of nostalgia also carries into the EP’s sound, with early 2000s pop influences woven throughout the project. It’s no surprise, then, that Cantrall brought in hitmaker Tricky Stewart, best known for co-writing Grammy-winning hits like Rihanna’s “Umbrella” and Beyoncé’s “Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It).”

“Tricky made me feel like I had all the answers,” Cantrall says. “He told me to trust my intuition and empowered me to not second guess myself as an artist.”

Despite feeling nervous about entering the writing room and collaborating with such an established name in the industry, Cantrall said Stewart helped bring her ideas to the surface while building her confidence as a songwriter. Reflecting on their time in the studio, she recalled how encouraging Stewart was throughout the creative process, helping her feel more comfortable opening up and finding her voice.

entertainment.title: Mort Weiner, Veteran Label Executive, Dies at 92: ‘His Commitment to Artists and Our Industry Was Superb’
entertainment.summary: Over a career spanning nearly four decades, Weiner held senior positions in sales, promotion, marketing and distribution at several major record labels.
entertainment.body:
Veteran record label executive Mort Weiner died on Oct. 25 at age 92. Over a career spanning nearly four decades, Weiner held senior positions in sales, promotion, marketing and distribution at several major record labels, including Columbia, MGM, Metromedia, Motown, RCA and 20th Century-Fox Records.

Veteran music executive Neil Portnow , former president/CEO of the Recording Academy, tells Billboard , “Mort was a colleague from my first days in L.A. at RCA in the late ‘70’s, and then at 20th Century Fox Records where I hired him to run our marketing, sales and international efforts. I couldn’t have made a better choice because his work, energy and commitment to artists and our industry were superb. But most importantly, I gained a true friendship which has lasted through these many decades. He will be missed by all who had the privilege to work with and know him.”

Weiner began his record company career in 1961 as the Miami branch manager for Dot Records, which had a No. 1 hit on the Billboard Hot 100 that year with Pat Boone ’s “Moody River.” He went on to handle local promotion for Columbia Records in Miami, where he helped build early interest in Simon & Garfunkel. In 1966, he took responsibility for promotion across 11 Southern states for Columbia’s Date label. He joined MGM and was named national singles sales manager for Verve and Verve/Forecast in 1967. Weiner joined Metromedia Records around the time of its launch in late 1968 and rose from Eastern regional promotion to director of national sales and then to national director of marketing and merchandising. The label’s biggest star was Bobby Sherman , one of the top teen pop stars of the era. Sherman landed four top 10 Hot 100 hits for Metromedia from 1969-70, including “Easy Come, Easy Go” and “Julie, Do Ya Love Me.” Weiner joined Motown Records in its Los Angeles office, where he served as executive administrator of promotion. His tenure included the label’s Anthology franchise, which drew on Motown’s priceless catalog. The Anthology series began in 1973 with a Temptations collection that rode the Billboard 200 for six months and went platinum. While at Motown, Weiner was named a finalist for record company executive of the year at Bobby Poe ’s Radio/Record Seminar and Awards Banquet. In 1975, Weiner moved to RCA as the sales and promotion manager for custom labels. He went on to direct custom label sales and, in 1977, became director of pop product merchandising, overseeing RCA’s pop product managers. His work with affiliated labels included Silver Convention’s “Fly, Robin, Fly” on Midland International (a Hot 100-topping, Grammy-winning smash from 1975), the soundtrack to The Omen on Tattoo Records, and releases by The Whispers and Carrie Lucas on Soul Train Records. Jefferson Starship thanked him in the credits to its 1978 album Earth , which made the top five on the Billboard 200 and went platinum. In 1979, Weiner joined 20th Century-Fox Records as director of sales and merchandising. He became vp of sales and merchandising in 1980. That same year, label president Portnow put him in charge of international operations. As part of the label’s push to expand sales abroad, Weiner met with executives at RCA, which handled the label’s international distribution. In an October 1980 Billboard interview, Portnow pointed to singer-songwriter Jim Photoglo ’s success in Japan as an example of the label’s increased presence overseas. Weiner later served as vp of sales and distribution at Total Experience Records, where he helped introduce a program that used lower suggested retail prices and dealer incentives to support new artists. He returned to Motown in 1987 as vp of sales and distribution, a newly created position at the time. Smokey Robinson had back-to-back top 10 hits on the Hot 100 that year: “Just to See Her” (which won a Grammy) and “One Heartbeat.” Weiner’s later work took him into record and CD manufacturing, including a role as vp of sales at Nimbus Manufacturing. From his early days promoting singles in Miami to his work in national distribution and CD manufacturing, Weiner spent his career on the business side of getting music heard.

entertainment.summary: "Kiss of the Spider Woman" cost $30 million to produce and earned less than $1.8 million at the worldwide box office.
entertainment.body:
Jennifer Lopez blamed an alleged lack of a sufficient marketing budget for her 2025 adaptation of “Kiss of the Spider Woman” bombing at the box office.

During Thursday’s episode of The New York Times’ “Popcast” podcast , Lopez, who starred in the musical drama alongside Tonatiuh and Diego Luna, reflected on the film’s disappointing performance while answering a question about a time things hadn’t gone her way in her career.

“I would have liked to have had a bigger marketing budget for ‘Kiss of the Spider Woman,'” she said while promoting her upcoming concert special, “The JLO Show.”

“I think it was underseen, and I also had higher hopes for it when I first started the project. It was such a great role for me,” she added.

Lopez, 57, went on to acknowledge that while the film’s marketing may have contributed to its poor performance, she also felt its execution fell short of expectations.

“Kiss of the Spider Woman,” which was based on John Kander and Fred Ebb’s 1993 Tony Award-winning Broadway musical of the same name, cost Lionsgate, Roadside Attractions and LD Entertainment $30 million to produce . Page Six has reached out to the studios for comment.

At the time of its release, the film — which was written and directed by Bill Condon — was expected to earn a modest $2 million at the box office during its opening weekend. Ultimately, it grossed less than $1.8 million worldwide.

Elsewhere during the podcast, Lopez addressed what she believes are misconceptions about her career as an actress.

sports.body:
“ I want a dome ,” Mayor Charelle L. Parker said on 93.3 WMMR, via the Philadelphia Inquirer . “Don’t you tell. This is a secret between us. I just saw a rendering of this beautiful dome that they’re talking about for the Bears.”

Moving into a dome would change the character of late-season and playoff games in Philadelphia, which are often affected by snow, wind and cold. Plenty of fans won’t like it. But politicians and NFL owners often prefer stadiums with roofs because they bring in lucrative events, indoor sports, concerts, conventions and trade shows.

The Eagles told season ticket holders last year that they are looking at either renovations to Lincoln Financial Field or a new stadium . Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie has committed only to staying in “the region,” not in the city of Philadelphia, but both Parker and Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro have said they want the Eagles to remain in the city.

The Eagles’ lease at Lincoln Financial Field runs through the 2032 season.

sports.title: Jaguars saw something in Liam Coen that other teams didn't
sports.summary: The Jaguars identified Coen as their No. 1 candidate and re-shaped their front office to get him, at a time when other teams weren't even interviewing him.
sports.body:
Coen’s great success should have other teams that hired new head coaches in 2025 asking themselves: What did we miss? Because the Jaguars were so high on Coen that he was their No. 1 target and they were willing to do whatever it took to get him, while no other team even bothered to give Coen an interview.

During the 2025 NFL coaching search , we tracked dozens of reports of head coaching interviews and requests among the seven teams that had vacancies. The Jaguars were the only team that so much as asked Coen to interview.

This week there’s been some media scrutiny on the Jets, who hired Aaron Glenn without considering Coen as a candidate. Glenn is 5-22; Coen is 20-6. But it’s unfair to single out the Jets for failing to interview Coen, because no team other than the Jaguars did, either.

The 41-year-old Coen had a résumé that should have made him a good candidate. NFL teams area always on the lookout for coaches who can nurture a franchise quarterback and run an innovative offense. Coen played quarterback at UMass and coached quarterbacks in college before getting hired by Sean McVay to work on the Rams’ staff, eventually became the Rams’ offensive coordinator under McVay, and had been a successful playcaller as offensive coordinator for the Buccaneers, as well as at Kentucky. With that background, it’s surprising that only the Jaguars wanted him.

And the Jaguars really wanted him, to the point that they were willing to do whatever it took to hire him. Coen initially turned the Jaguars down and agreed to a contract extension to stay with the Buccaneers, but Jaguars owner Shad Khan wouldn’t take no for an answer. When Coen said he was concerned about the direction of the Jaguars’ front office, Khan fired General Manager Trent Baalke and agreed to reshape the front office in a way that Coen would approve of if Coen would take the job. Coen was persuaded to take the Jaguars job, and the Jaguars later hired James Gladstone, who had worked with Coen on the Rams, as GM.

The result has been the Jaguars going from one of the worst teams in the NFL to one of the best. Coen’s success in Jacksonville has justified the faith Khan had in him. And raises questions about the total lack of interest from the rest of the league.
