sports.title: Bud Dupree requests release from Chargers, who haven't granted it
sports.summary: As the season continues to unfold — and as the trade deadline fades into the rear-view mirror — unhappy players have only one option: To request a release.
sports.body:
Via Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, Chargers linebacker Bud Dupree has done that . The Chargers, however, have not granted the request.

Dupree, per Fowler, also requested his release before the season.

It’s unknown whether the Chargers tried to trade him. His playing time has systematically dropped this year. He had no defensive snaps in two straight games before he was a healthy scratch in the Week 10 Monday night game against the Ravens.

That move came three days after Dupree had some pointed comments for the front office.

“Don’t ask hard questions to us; ask hard questions to them,” Dupree said. “Ask the hard questions. Everybody pull they cameras out and g o upstairs and ask questions to them. Everybody. Walk upstairs and ask them .”

Dupree is under contract, so there’s nothing he can do to force his way out. Still, the situation underscores the one-way nature of these deals.

The team can cut the player whenever it wants. The player can’t get out unless the team is willing to let him go.

sports.title: Nicolas Cage on his John Madden misfire: "I'm not Frank Caliendo"
sports.summary: This whole thing is antithetical to my identity.
sports.body:
That’s the one line that resonates most strongly in the new Madden movie. Because it’s exactly what John Madden would say if he saw it.

It’s bad. It’s very bad. Anyone who says it’s good has no taste and/or an agenda that involves the strategic application of lips to asses.

The biggest problem is Nicolas Cage as John Madden. Anyone who vividly remembers the unique charisma of John Madden knows instantly that nothing about Cage’s portrayal reflects the true nature, spirit, and demeanor of one of the most important and impactful figures in the entire history of the sport of football.

Cage, who seems to realize that his portrayal missed not only the bull’s-eye but also the entire wall on which the dart board was mounted, has defended the outcome by peering down his nose at the sports world.

“ He was not on my radar ,” Cage said of Madden, via Kirsten Chuba of the Hollywood Reporter . “I was growing up watching black-and-white Orson Welles movies and Fellini movies and Bruce Lee. I wasn’t interested in team sports whatsoever.”

“I’m someone that likes to stay out of his comfort zone and take a risk, I said yes, because that would be a transformation,” Cage explained regarding the decision to attempt to play the towering, iconic figure. “It would be something where I might learn a few things, taking on this character who is really nothing like me.”

The audience has learned that Cage’s interpretation is nothing like Madden.

“That’s what acting’s about,” Cage said. “I’m not an impressionist, I’m not Frank Caliendo. I lean more towards being a surrealist, meaning I like to get a concept of a personality and then dig deep and see what I can locate emotionally with my imagination and my psyche and filter it through the cadence and the appearance, within reason, of John Madden. I’m trying to give you an evocation, more or less, or an interpretation.”

sports.title: Colts officially place Daniel Jones on waivers
sports.summary: Daniel Jones is officially on the waiver wire.
sports.body:
The NFL transaction report has gone out this afternoon, and Jones appears as a waiver from the Colts. After the trade deadline, every player who gets released by his team has to go on waivers before he becomes a free agent.

That means any team that wants Jones on his current contract can claim him, but that is extraordinarily unlikely to happen. As the waiver transaction notes, Jones is a vested veteran with a fully guaranteed salary for the rest of this season. No team is going to want to claim that salary.

Once he clears waivers, however, he’ll be an unrestricted free agent, free to sign with any team, and it won’t be surprising if some team wants to add him for veteran depth. Jones has been terrible this season, but he’s been a competent starter at times in his career, and a team that wants an experienced backup may be interested in signing him for a minimal salary.

Jones was also waived almost exactly two years ago, on November 22, 2024. He cleared waivers and signed with the Vikings’ practice squad before signing with the Colts after that season.

sports.title: NFL will consider requiring minimum-night stays for international games
sports.summary: After the 49ers and the Rams took dramatically different approaches to their arrival in Melbourne for the first-ever Australia game, we raised the question of whether the league should require teams to get there early enough to advance the goal of promoting American football to international audienc
sports.body:
Via The Athletic , the NFL will consider adopting a minimum-night stay for teams playing internationally.

“Currently, we leave those football decisions on when the team arrives in the market to the club,” NFL executive V.P. of club business, major events, and international Peter O’Reilly told The Athletic . “It is something that we’ll consider moving forward on: Do we put some minimum nights in a market in there? It’s something we’ll look at.”

The league already does it for the Super Bowl, mandating a full-week experience that includes multiple press conferences, the annual “Opening Night” media extravaganza, and practicing at designated facilities.

“Having access to players and that type of experience when they’re in the market does have a lasting impact,” O’Reilly said. “That’s a factor when you start to think about encouraging or potentially looking at a policy where you’d want a club in the market for more than the day before.”

Beyond impacting strategic considerations, it would add to the total expense. The money would be worth it, if it further enhances the league’s overall reason for going global.

sports.title: Saints officially waive S Justin Reid
sports.summary: Safety Justin Reid already penned his good-bye missive to the Saints, but his departure did not become official until 4 p.m.
sports.body:
The Saints waived Reid on Friday, with the move made official on the NFL’s personnel notice.

Reid asked for his release this week, and the Saints have granted it.

“In life and sports, things don’t always go the way you planned or hoped they would,” Reid wrote on social media. “Unfortunately, this is one of those moments . But that doesn’t change the love and respect I have for this organization or city. I truly want to see this team and this city thrive. No one deserves it more than New Orleans and the Saints.”

He will go through waivers, with the NFL announcing at 4 p.m. ET on Monday whether he clears. If no team claims him, Reid will become a free agent.

Reid joined the Saints as a free agent in 2025, and he started all 24 games he played for the team. He had 118 tackles, an interception and a half-sack.

sports.title: Fan dies after falling during a fight at 49ers-Cowboys game
sports.summary: A man who attended Sunday's game between the 49ers and Cowboys has died due to injuries sustained in a fight during the game.
sports.body:
Via The Independent , 36-year-old Marco Narro was involved in an altercation with another fan near kickoff to the game. During the fight, Narro fell. After the incident, Narro stayed and watched the game.

During the game, he started to complain about pain. He and a friend sought attention from paramedics after the game. Narro was then transported to a local hospital.

The Arlington Police Department has opened a formal investigation. The prevalence of security cameras at AT&T Stadium should be useful when it comes to reconstructing the events.

The situation underscores one of the basic risks of engaging in fights at sporting events. It doesn’t take much to suffer, or to inflict, a very serious injury.

sports.summary: The New York Jets are, embarrassingly, a three-point underdog on Sunday against a team who didn’t earn their first win until less than a week ago. The Los Angeles Chargers will be looking to build on their 23-20 win over the Ravens, and the Jets are making the long trip out west to take them […]
sports.body: The New York Jets are, embarrassingly, a three-point underdog on Sunday against a team who didn’t earn their first win until less than a week ago. The Los Angeles Chargers will be looking to build on their 23-20 win over the Ravens, and the Jets are making the long trip out west to take them on. Here are six storylines to watch as New York seeks to inject some positivity into their season: Playing the slots Last week, we discussed the Jets’ varying options for their slot cornerback position and they eventually went with one of our suggestions, which was to primarily use Minkah Fitzpatrick there in nickel packages, bringing Malachi Moore off the bench to fill in at safety. The Jets potentially face a similar dilemma in the slot this week, albeit on offense. Both Omar Cooper and Isaiah Williams have been unable to practice, so if neither can go on Sunday, the Jets will have to make a change. One option could be to go with the guys currently on the roster. You could reactivate Jelani Woods and Tim Patrick and either run more multiple tight end packages, or use players like Garrett Wilson there. Another option could be to bring up Sterling Shepard or Jamaal Pritchett from the practice squad. The job share at running back remains a work in progress The Jets are still trying to figure out how to get the best out of Braelon Allen and Breece Hall now that both are healthy at the same time. Allen’s performances while Hall was out proved that he can benefit from a bigger workload. However, Hall brings different things to the table in the passing game, so the Jets will want him on the field more often than not. Last week was interesting because they employed Hall more in the passing game in the first half with Allen getting more carries. At the half, Allen had six carries and Hall had just two. However, after halftime, Allen carried the ball just twice and Hall had nine carries. It’s possible the Jets’ thinking was that Hall might produce better after halftime if he was fresh and the defense was tired. In the end, the pair had similar rushing numbers, but Hall produced more as a receiver. You can probably expect the Jets to keep working on this with one option being flipping last week’s gameplan on its head and using Hall early, then keeping Allen fresh to be the hammer in the second half. sports.title: Giants are Colts' next opponent, and John Harbaugh is taken aback by Daniel Jones news
sports.summary: Giants coach John Harbaugh is preparing right now for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
sports.body:
Harbaugh was visibly surprised at his press conference today when a reporter informed him that Jones has been released, and he said when asked about the work his advance scouts are doing on the Colts that it will certainly change things.

“Yeah, probably pretty dramatically,” Harbaugh said. “I mean, wow. I don’t want to get ahead of ourselves here. You just hit me with that.”

Harbaugh said the Giants will still watch plenty of tape of the Colts’ offense this season, but they’ll also have to watch tape of Anthony Richardson.

“The offense will be the offense they run, but it will be centered around the quarterback, for sure,” Harbaugh said. “And they’re probably different styles to some degree, so we’ll have to look at that when the time comes. We have people doing that this week. They’ll have to make a left turn, obviously. Thanks for the info.”

Richardson is a great athlete with a big arm, and the Colts loved him coming out of Florida, and he’ll now have until the end of the season to show whether he can in any way resemble the quarterback the Colts thought they were getting when they took him fourth overall in the 2023 NFL draft. Harbaugh’s Giants will be the first defense Richardson faces for his first meaningful playing time in two years.

[Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2123870179717525701?a=u-WIRR_AYd5r1qyc1oI&s=20] Ruled Out * CB Christian Benford * LB Dorian Williams This came as no surprise. The pair had not been able to practice all week. Soft tissue injuries usually take a little extra time to heal. And, if we had any hopes, head coach Joe Brady dashed those this morning when he announced their designation before Bills practice even began. Doubtful * TE Dalton Kincaid I would just read this as “Kincaid won’t play Sunday.” Now, I know, I said the same thing about Spencer Brown last week and he suited up and made a liar out of me. But Kincaid can rest. Josh Allen will have two (maybe three) other tight ends and six wide receivers to throw the ball too. Plus, there’s Ty Johnson. Kincaid resting and being full-strength on Thanksgiving night is the better choice. Questionable * S Damar Hamlin * TE Jackson Hawes * DL T.J. Sanders This is where that “maybe three” in the section above came from. If Hawes, who is dealing with some shoulder pain, is a go, that gives them plenty of reason to sit Kincaid. The surprise here is Hamlin. The safety showed up in a walking boot and on a scooter for Wednesday’s walkthrough. Then he was listed as a DNP on Thursday. Today, he was seen running. He’s definitely trying to prove his worth to a team that keeps adding and subtracting defensive backs around him. What we’re thinking I still think this could be the week we see Tre’Davious White. The Dolphins’ wide passing game isn’t exactly fear-inspiring, and it’s a good time to let Maxwell Hairston get some reps. But if he struggles, having the veteran in uniform could be what’s needed. Plus, it’s probably a good game to test White’s legs and see what he still has left in the tank. I’m also leading toward Shaq Thompson as well. The Bills don’t have a tight end on the practice squad, so the only other need this week is defensive secondary. Give the veterans some time – and some money – and test their game speed before the brutal Weeks 12 – 16 schedule hits. We will know tomorrow, if the Bills’ coaching staff agrees with me.

sports.body: This weekend, the Buffalo Bills square off against one of the franchise’s biggest foes, historically. In fact, some would say the Miami Dolphins are still Buffalo’s biggest rival. True or otherwise, to call Bills-Dolphins a heated rivalry at this juncture is doing more lip service to the past than the present. What is a fact is that Buffalo and Miami have alternated between lengthy spans of one-sided win streaks. Since the end of the 1980s, the Bills have largely had the Dolphins’ number. Sunday’s game at Highmark Stadium marks the 17th regular-season game for quarterback Josh Allen against Miami, a series that’s seen some of his most dominant play. Since Allen took over as QB1 in 2018, Buffalo is 14-3 against the Dolphins (including 1 playoff win). In 16 regular-season games, Allen has thrown for 4,256 yards with 42 touchdowns and nine interceptions, adding 703 rushing yards and another nine touchdowns on the ground. Let that sink in a moment as you consider the sort of stat line often associated with NFL MVP-winning quarterbacks. Dolphins week belongs to Josh Allen, and the latest matchup isn’t likely to change the narrative regardless of his final stat line. The oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook agree, where the majority among more than 200 currently available wager options predict favorable outcomes for Allen. Clearly, people expect Allen to put up significant stats in Week 11. If you stop for just a second and consider everything, Allen’s incredible history during this series rather than current trends may be shaping the favorable numbers. I believe Allen will have a strong game, perhaps running for a pair of touchdowns and throwing for a couple more scores. It’s his yardage where I’m hesitant to favor huge numbers. Allen’s again an MVP favorite for a reason, and the Dolphins are at a very different stage of team development compared to the Bills. Steichen also explained the timing by saying, “It’s just where we’re at in our season. . . . That’s just the situation that we’re at right now.”

The situation was clear. Jones was going to be benched, in order to ensure that he won’t suffer an injury that will trigger a $10.51 million guarantee for 2027. If that had happened, he would have been asked to be cut. And they likely would have done it.

sports.body: Look what we have here, Rumblers: It’s a primetime matchup between a pair of AFC teams. Though we’ve had a couple this season and more frequently of late, AFC vs. AFC is about as rare as a Barbary lion these days. The trouble here is that this is a terrible matchup, featuring teams that are decidedly anything other than apex hunters. That the NFL can still sell this product to anyone is an incredible feat. Yet football fans continue lining up to see awful teams take on each other. It’s not that this one is without some interest, which is due to a few star players among both Houston and Indianapolis. The issue is that as Buffalo Bills fans, you’re settling in to watch the 3-6 Texans take on the 3-7 Colts. Those two teams are a combined 6-13 — which, if you’ve done the math, is less total wins than the 8-1 Bills have on the season. Neither of these teams was supposed to flop this season, though the writing was on the wall for Indianapolis. But Houston? It’s been an epic collapse for the Texans in 2026. A once-mighty defense has proven feckless far too often this season, which has some saying that head coach DeMeco Ryans could be warming the very seat he sits on in Houston. Fair or not, the NFL is a production-based industry. If you’re like me, the game will be on simply because it helps fill the room a bit this evening. You may also share my passion for the Thursday Night Football crew, and their pre-/postgame coverage. If nothing else, there’s also the chances to see the Texans in their Nike Rivals uniforms — and yes, they sure did again steal the Oilers’ vibe. Are you looking for a reason to root on one team over the other here? What you favor depends on who to cheer on to victory. A Houston win helps Buffalo’s strength of schedule/strength of victory, which matters most for NFL teams with postseason hopes on life support. Instead, you may prefer seeing the Colts win simply so it “harms” the slotting of 2027 first-round pick they sent to the New York Jets. With that, here’s your open thread for Week 11 of Thursday Night Football. Maybe this one also turns into a decent game, like a few suspect snooze-fests in primetime before it. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills announced that they will retire wide receiver Andre Reed’s No. 83 jersey at some point during the 2027 NFL season. While the team did not announce when it will happen, they did announce that it will happen, giving fans the news that the retirement ceremony will happen sometime during next season. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBills/status/2123567003025784832?a=eiDWs2sPcy4ZrR46DXg&s=20] Reed is Buffalo’s franchise leader in targets (1,585), receptions (941), receiving yards (13,095), and receiving touchdowns (86). He played in Buffalo for 15 seasons, earning seven consecutive Pro Bowl nods from 1988-1994. He was named Second-Team All-Pro by the Associated Press in 1989 and 1990. A fourth-round draft choice out of Kutztown State University in Kutztown, PA, Reed was a key piece of a Buffalo team that made 10 playoff appearances, five AFC Championship Game appearances, and four Super Bowl appearances during his time with the franchise. At the time of his retirement, Reed ranked No. 3 all-time in receptions, and while he has since slipped to No. 23 all-time, it doesn’t dampen his accomplishments at all. A more pass-happy game has replaced the style of football played during Reed’s time in the league, making his numbers that much more impressive. Currently, Reed’s No. 83 jersey is worn by tight end Keleki Latu. Based on this announcement, it appears that Latu will need a new jersey number next year. Congratulations to Andre Reed—Go Bills! Watch Andre Reed learn that his jersey will be retired in a conversation with Bills’ owner Terry Pegula: [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBills/status/2123570266500706345?a=hUACLz3gES3lCd54MCs&s=20]

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills will play the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. The question right now is which Bills will actually play. Buffalo played their first of two straight divisional games last week and came back to Orchard Park with another win, but it may have cost them a significant portion of their roster. After a walkthrough practice on Wednesday, here’s what the Bills’ practice looked like today: [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2123529886702899498?a=q2z0msg8jWIlHqzpZ8g&s=20] Here’s What Changed * Dee Alford (concussion) - upgraded to Limited * Cole Bishop (shoulder) - upgraded to Full * Damar Hamlin (toe) - downgraded to DNP* * Jackson Hawes (shoulder) - downgraded to Limited* * T.J. Sanders (shoulder) - downgraded to Limited * O’Cyrus Torrence (personal) - returned to practice *On the report that Buffalo Bills PR published yesterday, Hamlin was listed as limited and Hawes was not listed at all. Today, the adjusted report shows today shows them as DNP and Limited respectively. Here’s What Stayed the Same * Christian Benford (groin) - DNP * Keon Coleman (ankle) - Full * Ray Davis (hamstring) - Limited * Amani Hooker (knee) - Limited * Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) - DNP * Ty Johnson (knee) - Full * Connor McGovern (neck) - Full * Tyrell Shavers (knee) - Full * Dorian Williams (calf) - DNP What We’re Watching The Bills defense is still looking thin despite the fact it looks as though Alford has progressed to the next step of the NFL’s concussion protocol. He will need a full practice on Friday and then no new symptoms on Saturday in order to completely clear the process and be ready to play. I would still look to see Tre’Davious White called up this weekend. The second practice squad elevation could go to Shaq Thompson. The veteran linebacker has been waiting for a game jersey this season, and with Williams not practicing for the second straight day, it looks like this could be the week. It’s also looking like the tight end room is struggling, but the Bills now have six wide receivers on the roster – plus they still have two more tight ends – so it’s doubtful they adjust much in their game plan.
